# What Are the California WARN Act 2026 Changes?

On Behalf Of Elite Trial Group| May 19, 2026 | FAQs

The California WARN Act 2026 changes expand what employers must put in writing when they lay off workers, close a worksite, or relocate operations. The new law, Senate Bill 617, took effect January 1, 2026 and amends California Labor Code Section 1401. It does not change the 60-day notice requirement. It changes what the notice must say.

Most workers getting handed a WARN notice in 2026 have no idea the rules shifted. They see the 60-day notice, sign for it, and start planning their last day. What they do not realize is that California now requires employers to include specific information about job placement services, food assistance benefits, and workforce development contacts. A notice that leaves any of this out is defective, and a defective notice can be the foundation of a WARN Act claim worth up to 60 days of back pay and benefits per affected worker.

This post breaks down what the California WARN Act 2026 changes require, what rights they create for workers, what employers are still getting wrong, and what to do if you received a notice that does not comply.
